# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none |
| callisto-format | MIT | model |
| callisto-vcs | MIT | model |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-conventional | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-changelog | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, vcs, manifests, format, changelog, conventional |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | all of the above |
| callisto-moon | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- MIT crates must never depend on FSL crates.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package <crate>:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive).
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

lastPrompt: Do we need to merge #124 first? Can we do this work in a git branch stack?

content.text:
No, #124 doesn't need to merge first. We can stack.

**Overlap:** wave 1 and #124 only share one file, `release/provider/mod.rs`: #124 removed the post-publish check methods, and wave 1 adds release notes to the GitHub-release operation. The wave 1 specs were also checked against #124's code. So base wave 1 on #124, not on `main`.

**The stack:**
```
main
└─ fix/release-run-simplify   #124
   └─ feat/release-parity      wave 1
      └─ …                     wave 2 onward, one branch per PR
```
Each PR targets the branch below it, so its diff only shows its own changes.

**The one catch:** we squash-merge. When a parent lands, the child still carries the parent's original commits, so it has to be restacked onto `main`. Two ways to handle that:
- **Graphite (`gt`),** which is installed. `gt sync` / `gt restack` rebases the whole stack after each merge, and `gt submit` keeps the PR bases right. The restack force-pushes the stacked branches, with lease, but only our own feature branches, never `main`.
- **Plain git:** merge `main` into the next branch after each merge. There's no force-push, but it adds merge commits (those disappear anyway with squash).

I'd use Graphite if you're fine with it restacking our own branches. Is the repo already set up with `gt`, or should I stick with plain git?

content.content:
Stacked PRs let you break a large change into a chain of pull requests
that build on each other. Use `gh stack` to create and manage your stack
locally, then push to GitHub to create your stack of PRs.

Usage:
  gh stack [command]

Examples:
  # Start a new stack targeting your default branch
  $ gh stack init

  # Or turn an existing set of branches into a stack
  $ gh stack init branch1 branch2 branch3

  # Make changes and commit, then add a branch to the stack
  $ gh stack add branch4

  # Push all branches and create/update PRs on GitHub
  $ gh stack submit

  # Keep your local in sync with remote
  $ gh stack sync

Stack management:
  add         Add a new branch on top of the current stack
  checkout    Checkout a stack by stack number, PR number, PR URL, or branch name
  init        Initialize a new stack
  modify      Interactively restructure a stack
  unstack     Remove a stack locally and on GitHub
  view        View the current stack

Remote operations:
  link        Link PRs into a stack on GitHub without local tracking
  merge       Merge a stack of pull requests
  push        Push active branches in the current stack to the remote
  rebase      Rebase a stack of branches
  submit      Create a stack of PRs on GitHub
  sync        Sync the current stack with the remote

content.content:
== init
Initialize a new stack of branches in the current repository.
You can pass multiple branch names to create a multi-layer stack in one
command. Existing branches are adopted automatically; missing branches are
created. By default, the first branch is based on the default branch, and
each subsequent branch is based on the previous one.
Use --base to specify a different trunk branch.
Usage:
  gh stack init [branches...] [flags]
== sync
Fetch, rebase, push, and sync PR state for the current stack.
This command performs a safe synchronization:
  1. Fetches the latest changes from the remote
  2. Reconciles the stack on GitHub with your local stack: pulls down
     branches for any PRs added to the stack on GitHub, or prompts you to
     resolve a divergence in an interactive terminal
  3. Fast-forwards the trunk branch to match the remote
  4. Cascade-rebases stack branches onto their updated parents
  5. Pushes all branches atomically (using --force-with-lease --atomic)
  6. Syncs PR state from GitHub
== rebase
Pull from remote and do a cascading rebase across the stack.
Ensures that each branch in the stack has the tip of the previous
layer in its commit history, rebasing if necessary.
Use --no-trunk to skip fetching and rebasing with the trunk branch.
Only the inter-branch rebases are performed (branch 2 onto branch 1,
branch 3 onto branch 2, etc.).
Usage:
  gh stack rebase [branch] [flags]
== merge
Merge some or all of a stack of pull requests using GitHub's atomic stack
merge. All members of the stack up to and including your chosen pull request are
merged into the base branch in a single, all-or-nothing operation: if any PR
cannot be merged, none are.
With no argument, the stack for the current branch is used. Pass a stack number
to merge a stack you don't have checked out, or a pull request number to merge
directly up to that PR. A bare number is treated first as a stack number, then
as a pull request number.
In an interactive terminal, a short wizard lets you choose how far up the stack
to merge (everything below your selection is always included), pick the merge

content.text:
GitHub's own stacked PRs work, via the official `gh stack` extension, which I've now installed. It solves the squash problem cleanly:
- **Setup:** `gh stack init fix/release-run-simplify` adopts #124 as the bottom of the stack. `gh stack add feat/release-parity` adds wave 1 on top, and so on for each wave. `gh stack submit` creates the PRs with the right bases.
- **Keeping it current:** `gh stack sync` fetches, rebases each branch onto its parent, and pushes (`--force-with-lease --atomic`, stack branches only, never `main`).
- **Merging:** `gh stack merge` merges the stack, up to whichever PR you choose, into `main` in one all-or-nothing operation. There's no manual restacking after a squash.

One thing to know: `sync` force-pushes our stack branches with lease. Earlier the safety check blocked a force-push, so the first `sync` may ask for your approval.

**Plan:**
1. Adopt #124 as the base of the stack.
2. Add wave 1 (correctness parity) on top and build it.
3. Add each later wave as its own layer.
4. You merge with `gh stack merge` whenever you're ready: all of it, or up to any PR.

#125 (specs) is docs only and independent, so it can merge on its own anytime.

Start the stack and wave 1?

Practical effect: it's not just this e2e test — any callisto user with a `[registries.pypi] url = "https://private-index..."` (Artifactory/Nexus/devpi/pypiserver) hits this same failure in production today, unconditionally. `--skip-existing` needs to become conditional (omitted whenever `index` is `Some`, i.e. a non-default registry) for private-PyPI publish to work at all.

content.text:
The end-to-end work found a real bug. callisto always passes `--skip-existing` to `twine upload`, and current twine refuses that flag for any index except pypi.org and test.pypi.org. So every private PyPI registry (Artifactory, Nexus, devpi, pypiserver) fails to publish today. The agent confirmed it against a real local pypiserver, and I confirmed it in the code.

**The fix, authorized in this layer:** pass `--skip-existing` only for pypi.org and test.pypi.org. The release path already checks the registry before publishing, so other indexes don't need it. It lands as its own commit with a changeset, and then the PyPI end-to-end test.

The npm end-to-end test already worked for real against a local Verdaccio, configured only through `.npmrc`.

`Tag` -> `ForgeRelease` (create as draft) -> every `ArtifactUpload` -> `ForgePublish`. `ForgePublish` depends on the draft and on *every* upload of that release, including when there are none.

-- `ForgeRelease` effect: `gh release create TAG --repo R --verify-tag --draft`, with `--notes-file` holding the package's `## VERSION` changelog section, or `--generate-notes` plus a `notes: using generated notes (<reason>) for <package>` stderr line when none is usable (`ReleaseNotes`, derived at execution and outside the intent digest), plus `--prerelease` when the released version has a semver pre-release part (`Version::is_prerelease()`, the same source as the npm `next` dist-tag).

+- `ForgeRelease` effect: `gh release create TAG --repo R --verify-tag --draft --generate-notes`, plus `--prerelease` when the released version has a semver pre-release part (`Version::is_prerelease()`, the same source as the npm `next` dist-tag).

- Lookup: `GET /releases/tags/{tag}` omits drafts, so a 404 there is followed by a bounded scan of `GET /releases?per_page=100&page=N` (at most 10 pages). Both roles and the upload role share this one lookup.

- `ForgeRelease` is `Exact` for a draft or a published release; `ForgePublish` is `Exact` only when `draft: false` and `Absent` while still a draft. A release whose tag matches but whose `prerelease` flag disagrees with the version is `Conflict { ForgeReleasePrereleaseDiffers }`.

import re,json,subprocess
files=subprocess.check_output(["git","diff","--name-only","--diff-filter=U"],text=True).split()
pat=re.compile(r"<<<<<<< [^\n]*\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n",re.S)
def note(b):

for f in files:
    s=open(f).read()
    def res(m):
        base,rebased=m.group(1),m.group(2)
        a,b=note(base),note(rebased)
        notes=[n for n in (a,b) if n]
        merged=" ".join(dict.fromkeys(notes))
        keep=[l for l in rebased.splitlines(keepends=True) if '"revision_note"' not in l]
        ind=re.match(r'(\s*)',rebased or base).group(1) or "  "
        if merged: keep.append(f'{ind}"revision_note": {json.dumps(merged)}\n')
        return "".join(keep)
    s=pat.sub(res,s); json.loads(s); open(f,"w").write(s); print("resolved",f)

lines: -**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

-Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.

-The forge destination moves to `forge-repository = "owner/repo"` directly under `[release]`. Each publish target uses its own registry key (`[registries.<key>]` or the built-in default). A legacy `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is still read when the new key is absent.
-- `--profile` is removed from `release plan` and `release execute`.
-- `[release.profiles.<name>]` other than `production` is rejected; `registry-routes` is ignored.
-- Setting both `[release].forge-repository` and a different `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is rejected.
-- Release intents are schema v5 and run envelopes v3; re-plan intents made by older versions.

-Release planning now rejects an untrusted or non-https npm `publishConfig.registry`, requires an unreleased npm platform dependency to be selected with its owner, orders dev-only dependency cycles instead of failing, publishes scoped npm packages as public by default, and uses the changelog section as GitHub release notes (falling back to generated notes with a stderr notice).

-- `--package` for a package with no pending release fails with "nothing pending to release"; one with no publish target fails with "no publish target"; a name not in the workspace is an unknown package.
-- `release plan` fails with E199 for a `publish-to` target it cannot dispatch (NuGet) instead of skipping it.

-`release execute` now adopts every effect that already landed, including a published registry version (one warning line each), and builds the receipt from in-memory execution state, so "Re-run failed jobs" finishes a partial release instead of failing with E174. Execution state is no longer persisted, and E173 and E174 are gone.
-- `release reconcile` and `callisto schema --type release-state` are removed.
-- The receipt's run envelope drops `kind` and is envelope schema v2.

content.text:
Fixed, and all 6 PRs are mergeable again. #126 now targets `main` and contains only its own commits.

**Why a stack can still conflict:** the stack wasn't the problem; the squash merge was. #124 was squash-merged by itself, which put one new commit on `main`. GitHub then retargeted #126 to `main`, but #126's branch still carried #124's original commits underneath its own. Git saw two different versions of the same changes and reported conflicts in every PR above it.

`gh stack rebase` recognised #124 as merged, dropped its old commits, and replayed the rest onto `main`. The code in every branch is identical to before.

**Avoiding it next time:** land PRs from the stack with `gh stack merge`, or GitHub's stack merge button, rather than squash-merging one PR on its own. If you do squash one on its own, tell me and I'll restack right away with `gh stack sync`.

The wave 4 review and wave 5a (CLI surface) are still running. Both were based on the pre-restack branches, but the content is identical, so I'll stack their work on the new tips.

lastPrompt: How can I merge the stack locally with an admin override? The web UI doesn't allow me to do so?

content.text:
`gh stack merge` can't do it. Its help says: *"Bypassing merge requirements is not supported for stacks."* So an admin override has to go one PR at a time, bottom up, with `gh pr merge --admin`, restacking after each squash:

```sh
gh stack checkout 127
for pr in 126 128 129 130 132 133; do
  gh pr merge "$pr" --admin --squash --delete-branch || break
  gh stack sync        # drops the merged commits, retargets and pushes the rest
done
```

Run it with the `!` prefix so the output lands here:

```
! gh stack checkout 127 && for pr in 126 128 129 130 132 133; do gh pr merge "$pr" --admin --squash --delete-branch || break; gh stack sync; done
```

Notes:
- **`--delete-branch`** makes GitHub retarget the next PR to `main`. `gh stack sync` then rebases it without the merged commits, the same fix as the conflict earlier.
- **`sync` force-pushes the remaining stack branches, with lease.** That's expected. If one hits a conflict it stops, and the `|| break` ends the loop so you can hand it to me.
- **Wave 4 (`feat/release-command`)** isn't a PR yet: its review was cut off by the outage and is still running. The loop stops at #133, and wave 4 goes on top afterwards.
- **To use the web UI next time:** add yourself or the admin role as a bypass actor on the `main` ruleset. Or turn off required approvals there while you're the only reviewer. Then `gh stack merge` works without overrides.

Want me to run the loop for you instead? It merges PRs into `main` using your admin rights, so it needs your explicit go.

- No path produces an effect without these guarantees. Gaps: M3 and L1.
- Design note: a local run can publish and tag an unpushed commit or a feature branch. This is allowed by the spec ("any branch").
2. Selection: M1, M2. Without `--package`, every unreleased dispatchable package is selected, prereleases included, and platform workspaces are refused.

content.text:
Yes. Merge commits solve it; rebase-merge only partly does.

| Method | What happens to the PRs above |
|---|---|
| Squash (today) | `main` gets one new commit that isn't in the child branches, so every PR above needs a restack. |
| Rebase and merge | `main` gets rewritten copies of the commits (new SHAs). The children still hold the originals. `git rebase` usually recognises identical patches, but GitHub's PR view can still show conflicts. It helps only partly. |
| **Merge commit** | The PR's own commits land on `main` unchanged, so every PR above is already based on them. GitHub just retargets the next PR to `main`: no restack, no force-push, no conflicts. |

**Recommendation:** enable merge commits in the repo settings and use them for stacked PRs (`gh pr merge --merge --admin`, or `gh stack merge --merge`). Keep squash for everything else if you like the tidy history.

**Trade-off:** `main` then shows each PR's individual commits plus a merge commit. That's harmless here. Changelogs come from changesets, not commit messages, and our commits are already conventional.

**One exception: keep squash for the release PR (#113).** I haven't verified that the release trust checks behave identically on a merge commit. They look at the merged commit's GitHub signature and its diff against its parent. I'd rather check that than guess.

With merge commits, your admin loop becomes:
```
! for pr in 126 128 129 130 132 133; do gh pr merge "$pr" --merge --admin || break; done
```

content.text:
The exit codes are the one open question, and my spec made them contradictory. The agent's interpretation is:

| Exit | `status --check` meaning (as built) |
|---|---|
| 1 | errors |
| 2 | no errors, changesets pending |
| 3 | no errors, nothing pending |

So `--check` always exits non-zero, even when everything is fine. That's awkward for CI: every caller has to know that 2 and 3 mean success.

**A real consumer depends on the old codes:** michi's `release.yml` treats `status --check` exiting 1 as "changesets pending" and 2 as "none pending". Its release job is already broken, though, and will need updating regardless.

**My recommendation:** keep it conventional.
- `status --check` exits 0 with no errors and 1 with errors. It's a validation gate, which is what `validate` was.
- "Is anything pending?" goes in the output: JSON gets a `pending` count, and text shows it.
- Scripts like michi's use `callisto status --format json | jq '.pending'` instead of decoding exit codes.

Go with the conventional 0/1 codes? I'll have the agent switch them, simplify the action, and update michi's workflow in the same pass.

lines: +**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

+Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.

+Add discoverable --help surface (8 user commands, plumbing hidden), NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR-driven color and box-drawing tables for status and release --dry-run, and remove schema-version text from default output.
+**`callisto release` replaces the legacy publish commands**

+`callisto release` publishes, tags, and creates GitHub releases for every package whose current version has no tag, from any branch with a clean worktree. `--dry-run` previews the plan anywhere; `--package` restricts it and keeps fixed and linked group members together; an unreleased runtime, optional, or peer dependency must be selected with its dependent; credentials (including alternate cargo registries, credential providers, `.npmrc` and `.pypirc`) are checked before the first effect; the receipt goes to the platform state dir or `--receipt`, never inside the checkout.
+- Removed `callisto publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag` (including `--floating-major`), and `filter-plan`. Use `callisto release` or `callisto release --dry-run`.

+- Removed graph `plan_publish`, `filter_plan_by_report`, `create_tags`, `toposort::publish_order`; moon extension `plan-publish` is now `release`, and removed names error instead of falling back to `status`.

+- `release plan --package` now also keeps config-declared linked-group members, and both routes refuse an unselected unreleased dependency (`ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason::DependencyNotSelected`, was `PlatformDependencyNotSelected`).
+- Release decisions are written as schema 2 (adds `unreleasedVersion`). Schema 1 files still read; an earlier build cannot read a schema-2 decision.

+The forge destination moves to `forge-repository = "owner/repo"` directly under `[release]`. Each publish target uses its own registry key (`[registries.<key>]` or the built-in default). A legacy `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is still read when the new key is absent.
+- `--profile` is removed from `release plan` and `release execute`.
+- `[release.profiles.<name>]` other than `production` is rejected; `registry-routes` is ignored.
+- Setting both `[release].forge-repository` and a different `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is rejected.
+- Release intents are schema v5 and run envelopes v3; re-plan intents made by older versions.

<teammate-message teammate_id="review-wave6" color="pink" summary="Wave 6 review: 1 P0 root-discovery bug, rest clean">
feat/setup-core review complete (diff vs origin/feat/cli-surface, worktree removed, no edits made).

**Commands run (all green):**
- `cargo test -p callisto-manifests`: 204 passed
- `cargo test -p callisto-graph`: 645 passed
- `cargo test -p callisto-cli`: 294 passed
- `cargo test -p callisto-moon`: 30 passed
- `cargo clippy -p <each> --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: 0 warnings, all 4
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean

**Manual e2e (built target/debug/callisto):** fresh single-crate repo (no commit → init → commit → release --dry-run), two-crate cargo workspace with binary shipping via `--artifact-target`/`--forge-repository`, npm single-package with `bin`, AC-008 (already-initialized/E190), AC-011/E192 (no origin), AC-011b/E191 (not git), AC-012a (ambiguous tag convention/E193), AC-003b forge mismatch (E187) and invalid-forge-string, AC-019 (tagged version excluded from preview). In every case the init preview text matched `release --dry-run` verbatim, and error paths wrote nothing.

## P0 — root-discovery fallback has no repository boundary, silently binds to an unrelated ancestor manifest

`crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/root.rs:9-21`, `find_workspace_root`'s new `nearest(is_package_root)` fallback walks `canonical.ancestors()` with **no stopping bound** — not the git toplevel, not even the .git directory it's sitting in. It just returns the nearest ancestor holding a Cargo.toml `[package]`/package.json/pyproject.toml, however far up the filesystem that is.

Two confirmed repros (built binary, not just reasoning):

1. **Vendored/nested package picked instead of the real root.** Single-package cargo repo, run from inside `vendor/some-dep/` (its own `Cargo.toml [package]`, no `[workspace]` anywhere): `callisto status` reports only `some-dep 0.1.0`, ignoring the real `myapp` package entirely. `callisto --dry-run init --yes --versioning independent` run from that same directory detects only `some-dep`, and would write `vendor/some-dep/callisto.toml` — inside the vendored tree — on a real run. Before this diff, this case had no fallback and would correctly error `WorkspaceRootNotFound`; now it silently succeeds with the wrong root.

2. **Escapes the git repository boundary entirely.** Directory layout: `homelike2/package.json` (unrelated, e.g. simulating a stray `$HOME/package.json`) → `homelike2/proj/` (real git repo, `origin` set, no manifest anywhere inside it) → `homelike2/proj/docs/`. Running `callisto status` from `proj/docs/` climbs straight past the actual git root and binds to `homelike2/package.json`, reporting package `home-global-scripts 1.0.0` — a completely unrelated package outside the repository — with exit 0 and no warning (git's own "not a git repository" stderr leaks but doesn't block anything). `callisto init` in the same spot fails with E191 "not a Git repository" naming the *wrong* (outer) path, which is at least safe, but any read command (`status`, `release --dry-run`, etc.) silently succeeds against the wrong project.

This affects every command, not just `init` — `crates/callisto-cli/src/workspace.rs` routes both `load_workspace` and the new `workspace_root` (used by `init`) through the same `find_workspace_root`. It's a correctness bug for reads and a real filesystem-safety concern for `init` specifically, since a non-dry-run could scaffold `callisto.toml` into a directory the user never intended (a vendored dep, node_modules, or an unrelated ancestor).

Fix direction: bound the package-root fallback (and arguably the workspace-root search too) to the git repository's toplevel — e.g. resolve `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first and never climb past it — and within that bound prefer the outermost matching manifest over the nearest, so a nested vendor/node_modules manifest can't shadow the real project root.

## Everything else: no findings
- Config written (AC-005/007/009/009a/010/012/019/023): minimal, valid TOML via `toml_edit`, `resolve_config_text` round-trips, preview matches `release --dry-run` byte-for-byte in every manual run.
- Tag-convention detection (AC-012/012a/012b): matches spec exactly, including the v{version} exclusivity rule; verified E193/E194 paths.
- Error cases: every error path I hit (E187-E196, InitRequiresYes, InitMissingFlags) named the fix and wrote nothing (`nothing_written` checked on disk, not just asserted in-process).
- `--dry-run` global flag: detects, asks, previews, writes nothing — confirmed.
- bin-name derivation (AC-009a) in `callisto-manifests/{cargo,npm,python}.rs`: matches spec precisely (first `[[bin]]` or package name via src/main.rs; npm string unscoped name or object keys; PyPI `[project.scripts]` keys).
- Style: error.rs comments are one line; new diagnostic codes E187-E199 checked for collisions across the crate — none found; changeset (`.changeset/init-first-run-setup.md`) is succinct, states breaking changes plainly, no Claude-Session trailer; `render/mod.rs` cleanly drops the old reconcile-diff rendering.
- `callisto-moon/src/extension_pdk.rs`: rewritten to call `init::write`/`write_changeset_readme` directly (no prompts on that host surface) — matches the removed `InitOptions`/reconcile API; `Workspace::load` before the file-exists check is safe since `config::load` already treats a missing `callisto.toml` as `RawConfig::default()`, pre-existing behavior, not new.

Everything else in the diff (release/local.rs, release/mod.rs export refactor, model/report.rs InitReport shape, fixtures scaffold_callisto helper) is mechanical and consistent with the spec's non_goals boundary with SPEC-DX-CONFIG-RELEASE-SCHEMA.
</teammate-message>

lines: -**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

-Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.
-**`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**

-`init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.

-Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `vendor/` or `node_modules/` packages never shadow it.
-- `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
-- A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
-- `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
-- Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.
-- A forge repository other than `origin`'s GitHub repository is refused.
-- The written config holds only answers: no `[changesets]`, `[cascade]`, or `[init]` defaults.

-Add discoverable --help surface (8 user commands, plumbing hidden), NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR-driven color and box-drawing tables for status and release --dry-run, and remove schema-version text from default output.
-**`callisto release` replaces the legacy publish commands**

-`callisto release` publishes, tags, and creates GitHub releases for every package whose current version has no tag, from any branch with a clean worktree. `--dry-run` previews the plan anywhere; `--package` restricts it and keeps fixed and linked group members together; an unreleased runtime, optional, or peer dependency must be selected with its dependent; credentials (including alternate cargo registries, credential providers, `.npmrc` and `.pypirc`) are checked before the first effect; the receipt goes to the platform state dir or `--receipt`, never inside the checkout.
-- Removed `callisto publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag` (including `--floating-major`), and `filter-plan`. Use `callisto release` or `callisto release --dry-run`.

-- Removed graph `plan_publish`, `filter_plan_by_report`, `create_tags`, `toposort::publish_order`; moon extension `plan-publish` is now `release`, and removed names error instead of falling back to `status`.

-- `release plan --package` now also keeps config-declared linked-group members, and both routes refuse an unselected unreleased dependency (`ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason::DependencyNotSelected`, was `PlatformDependencyNotSelected`).
-- Release decisions are written as schema 2 (adds `unreleasedVersion`). Schema 1 files still read; an earlier build cannot read a schema-2 decision.

-The forge destination moves to `forge-repository = "owner/repo"` directly under `[release]`. Each publish target uses its own registry key (`[registries.<key>]` or the built-in default). A legacy `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is still read when the new key is absent.
-- `--profile` is removed from `release plan` and `release execute`.
-- `[release.profiles.<name>]` other than `production` is rejected; `registry-routes` is ignored.
-- Setting both `[release].forge-repository` and a different `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is rejected.
-- Release intents are schema v5 and run envelopes v3; re-plan intents made by older versions.

- Added `InitFacts.has_platform_packages: bool`, computed in `detect()` using the exact same predicate `ci_release_route` already uses (`is_platform_package(package) || workspace.identity.platforms_of(&package.id).next().is_some()`), so both routes now agree.
- `needs_workflow_matrix` now reads that field instead of scanning `facts.packages` for `platform: true`.
- Added a regression test that builds a real Case-E fixture (owner `package.json` with `optionalDependencies` naming a sibling `os`/`cpu`-tagged platform package.json, no Cargo/npm binary at all) through the real `detect()` path, asserts the platform package does NOT become its own `InitPackage`, and asserts `has_platform_packages`/`needs_workflow_matrix` still catch it. lines: +**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

+Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.

+`callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/release.yml` for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`/`--no-workflow` (mutually exclusive), refuses to overwrite an existing file (checked before the preview, including under `--dry-run`). Passing `--workflow` for a build-matrix workspace errors naming the reason; the interactive question is skipped instead, with a note that also lands in `InitReport.diagnostics` (`workflow-generation-needs-matrix`) for `--format json` callers. The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.

lines: -**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

-Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.

-`callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (the workflow path release artifact attestations are bound to) for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`/`--no-workflow` (mutually exclusive), refuses to overwrite an existing file (checked before the preview, including under `--dry-run`). The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.

-`callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the accepted values. Its environment-setup step no longer references sibling action `setup-callisto` through `uses:` (`$/` and an external `owner/repo/path@ref` both resolve against whichever ref invoked the *top-level* workflow, not necessarily this action's own) -- it now calls `setup-callisto`'s install script directly by `github.action_path`, so it always uses its own checked-out ref, including when invoked from another repository's workflow.
-**`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**

-`init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.

-Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `vendor/` or `node_modules/` packages never shadow it.
-- `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
-- A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
-- `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
-- Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.
-- A forge repository other than `origin`'s GitHub repository is refused.
-- The written config holds only answers: no `[changesets]`, `[cascade]`, or `[init]` defaults.

-Add discoverable --help surface (8 user commands, plumbing hidden), NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR-driven color and box-drawing tables for status and release --dry-run, and remove schema-version text from default output.
-**`callisto release` replaces the legacy publish commands**

-`callisto release` publishes, tags, and creates GitHub releases for every package whose current version has no tag, from any branch with a clean worktree. `--dry-run` previews the plan anywhere; `--package` restricts it and keeps fixed and linked group members together; an unreleased runtime, optional, or peer dependency must be selected with its dependent; credentials (including alternate cargo registries, credential providers, `.npmrc` and `.pypirc`) are checked before the first effect; the receipt goes to the platform state dir or `--receipt`, never inside the checkout.
-- Removed `callisto publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag` (including `--floating-major`), and `filter-plan`. Use `callisto release` or `callisto release --dry-run`.

-- Removed graph `plan_publish`, `filter_plan_by_report`, `create_tags`, `toposort::publish_order`; moon extension `plan-publish` is now `release`, and removed names error instead of falling back to `status`.

-- `release plan --package` now also keeps config-declared linked-group members, and both routes refuse an unselected unreleased dependency (`ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason::DependencyNotSelected`, was `PlatformDependencyNotSelected`).
-- Release decisions are written as schema 2 (adds `unreleasedVersion`). Schema 1 files still read; an earlier build cannot read a schema-2 decision.

Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="review-wave7b" color="blue" summary="wave7b matrix workflow review complete">
Reviewed feat/setup-matrix (diff vs feat/setup-workflow) adversarially. Worktree removed.

**Commands (real runs, not inferred):**
- `cargo test -p callisto-graph`: 670 passed (27 suites)
- `cargo test -p callisto-cli`: 309 passed (31 suites)
- `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p callisto-cli --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- `actionlint` (incl. `-shellcheck=shellcheck`) on the oxc sample: no findings
- `zizmor --offline` on the oxc sample: no findings (1 ignored/10 suppressed — the artipacked ignore on execute's checkout, matching the reference workflow's own pattern)

**HIGH — weakened release-authorization gate vs. callisto-release.yml.** The matrix template's only gate is `release_decision.rs`'s `derive_release_commit_decision`, whose own doc comment states: "GitHub-specific PR/approval provenance belongs in the workflow boundary; this graph function verifies the local, provider-neutral commit delta only." The hand-written `callisto-release.yml` supplies that missing half via `release-candidate` (lines 97–151): GitHub API check that the commit is a *merged, GitHub-verified-signed* PR from a `callisto/version-packages*` branch. The generated matrix workflow (init.rs `MATRIX_WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE`, ~line 156) supplies only a content precondition (decision file added/modified vs. `HEAD^`). I traced the actual bar in `derive_release_commit_decision` (release_decision.rs:316-470): it requires a coherent version bump + changelog touch + ≥1 changeset consumed + decision digest match — real work, not a one-line forge — but nothing checks *who* authored the commit or that it went through the bot/PR/signature path. Net effect: anyone with write access to the trigger branch who can construct that coherent diff (no PR, no review, no signature) triggers plan→build→execute with `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN` in scope. The spec's revision_note (points 6-7) acknowledges relying on "execution-time idempotency" instead — but idempotency (can't double-release) and authorization (who may trigger) are different guarantees, and the note doesn't seem to register that gap. Given AC-008a explicitly scoped this out as "by design," this reads as a recorded decision rather than an oversight — but I'd confirm the team actually weighed the authorization-vs-idempotency distinction before signing off, since it's a real behavioral regression from the reference workflow's trust model.

**MEDIUM — missing `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`.** The `execute` job (init.rs, MATRIX_WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE, execute job's permissions ~line 295-ish / sample workflow.yml:176) grants `id-token: write`, and docs/06-publishing.md:110 is explicit: "Publish npm packages with provenance from GitHub Actions: give the execute job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package... Callisto needs no flag." The generated execute env block (sample workflow.yml:223-226 / init.rs `secrets` vec, render_workflow ~line 934-946) only sets `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN` — never `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`. Since BuildMatrix's whole purpose is napi/npm platform packages, `id-token: write` is granted but functionally inert: no npm provenance attestation actually happens. Fix: add `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` to the execute env whenever the workspace has an Npm ecosystem package in the BuildMatrix shape (mirrors the existing `secrets.push(...)` pattern in `render_workflow`, callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:934-941).

**LOW/INFO — asymmetric attestation coverage.** `build` job's `actions/attest-build-provenance` step runs only `if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'` (sample:157-160); napi `.node` outputs are uploaded and later consumed by `execute`'s "Place napi artifacts" step with zero attestation or digest verification before they feed `npm publish`. This mirrors an existing asymmetry already in the model (`ArtifactManifestV1`/`ArtifactSlotId` only exist for `[[release.artifact]]` cargo slots — see callisto-model/src/release.rs:1330-1520; no equivalent typed attestation binding exists anywhere for platform/napi packages). Not introduced by this diff and explicitly SPEC-DX-RELEASE-CLI territory, but worth a tracked follow-up since it's the same publish path handling real secrets.

**LOW — `callisto matrix`'s new artifact-resolution silently drops unmatched packages.** crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs:56-62: `.filter_map(|artifact| { let (package, manifest) = all_packages.iter().find_map(...)? ...})` — if a `[[release.artifact]] package =` name doesn't resolve to any workspace package (typo, wrong ecosystem), the slot is just dropped from `platformTargets` with no diagnostic and no error, unlike the sibling `UnrecognisedPlatformTriple` warning path a few lines below in matrix.rs:46-57 for a bad triple on a resolved package. Contrast with `derive.rs`'s `ReleaseArtifactOwnerNotReleased` error for the same class of problem in the real release-plan path. Practical blast radius is limited — the generated workflow's plan-job jq has `// error("callisto matrix has no entry for artifact slot ...")` as a backstop, so CI still fails loudly, just one layer downstream of where `callisto matrix` run standalone (or via `init`'s `detect()`) could have said so directly. Consider a diagnostic here for parity with the triple case.

**Correctness vs. callisto-release.yml — everything else checked, no findings.** Content-precondition step correctly handles: orphan/first commit (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^` short-circuits false, no `set -e` trip inside the `if` test list), regular two-parent merge commits (`diff-tree parent HEAD` diffs against first parent only, which is the standard two-tree compare, not combined-diff display logic), and squash merges (single new parent, diff captures the whole squashed delta). Force-push doesn't break the detection mechanics themselves — it's subsumed by the HIGH finding above. `!cancelled()` + build/execute gating, `fail-fast: false`, concurrency group on execute, and the version-pr job body all match reference patterns.

**Matrix build — no findings.** 18-triple runner/cross table (matrix.rs, pre-existing, unchanged by this diff) is used consistently for both napi and cargo entries; windows uses `windows-latest` + bash-shell run steps with `tar`/`zip`-or-`7z` fallback (zip absent on windows-latest is handled); `cross --locked --version 0.2.5` pin matches `.github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh`'s own pin exactly. `--locked` is used on the cargo build step; napi build has no `--locked` equivalent, but that's napi-rs's own build model, not a callisto omission. One target failing fails the whole `build` job (no `continue-on-error`), which correctly blocks `execute` — same posture as reference. No caching in the build job, but the reference's own `build-artifact` job doesn't cache either, so not a regression.

**Security — template injection / secrets scoping: clean.** Grepped every `${{ }}` in the sample; all matrix-context values (`matrix.hostRunner`, `matrix.artifactName`, etc.) are consumed via `env:` blocks and referenced as `$VAR` inside `run:` bodies, never interpolated directly into script text — zizmor's injection audit agrees. Secrets (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`) appear only in `execute`'s env. `persist-credentials: false` everywhere except `execute`'s tag-push checkout, which is deliberately `true` with an explicit `# zizmor: ignore[artipacked]` comment — same pattern as the reference workflow.

**Style — no findings.** Comments are one line each; both changesets (`.changeset/sturdy-matrix-builds.md`, the trimmed `gentle-badgers-swim.md`) are succinct with no session-link trailer; E202/E203 both carry `miette::Diagnostic` code+help per AGENTS.md invariant 4; `write_workflow` still routes through `atomic_write` (unchanged call path, invariant 3 intact).

Also confirmed via the new `matrix_lists_release_artifact_cargo_binaries_beside_napi_targets` integration test (crates/callisto-cli/tests/cli_tests.rs) that AC-005 works end-to-end against the real `callisto` binary, not just unit-level string assertions.
</teammate-message>

content.text:
The review of #139 is done. The generated workflow is clean on permissions, secrets scoping, template injection and every correctness check against callisto's hand-written workflow. It found one decision for you and three smaller items.

**HIGH, and a decision for you:** the generated workflows trust branch protection, not the release PR. Callisto's own workflow also checks that a release commit is a GitHub-verified merge of the bot's release PR. The generated ones don't:
- **Matrix (#139):** it publishes when a push changes the release decision file. Anyone who can push to the default branch without review could trigger a publish.
- **Simple (#138):** the same applies. `callisto release` runs on every push, and publishes any version without a tag.

This is the same trust model as changesets/action and release-please: protect the default branch, and a merge is the approval. Two options:
- **(a) Match prior art:** document that the default branch must be protected, and have `init` print a one-line reminder when it generates a workflow. No extra machinery.
- **(b) Defense in depth:** the generated workflow also checks, through GitHub's API, that the commit is a merged release PR, as callisto's own workflow does. That's about 10 lines of YAML per workflow, but it ties the generated workflows to GitHub's API.

I'd go with (a), since it matches the zero-config goal and prior art.

**Fixing now, no decision needed:**
- **MEDIUM:** the matrix workflow grants `id-token: write` but never sets `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`, so npm provenance never actually happens. Adding it whenever npm packages exist.
- **LOW:** `callisto matrix` silently drops a `[[release.artifact]]` entry whose package doesn't exist. It will warn, the same way it already does for a bad target triple.
- **LOW, tracked follow-up:** napi `.node` files aren't attested before `npm publish`. That's an existing gap in the release model, not something this PR introduced.

lines: +**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

+Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.

+`callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (the workflow path release artifact attestations are bound to) for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`/`--no-workflow` (mutually exclusive), refuses to overwrite an existing file (checked before the preview, including under `--dry-run`). After writing the file, init prints that a merge to the default branch publishes, so that branch should require pull requests and reviews. JSON output carries the same text as a `workflow-merge-publishes` diagnostic with the new `info` severity. The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`; npm workspaces also set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so publishes carry provenance), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.

+`callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the accepted values. Its environment-setup step no longer references sibling action `setup-callisto` through `uses:` (`$/` and an external `owner/repo/path@ref` both resolve against whichever ref invoked the *top-level* workflow, not necessarily this action's own) -- it now calls `setup-callisto`'s install script directly by `github.action_path`, so it always uses its own checked-out ref, including when invoked from another repository's workflow.
+**`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**

+`init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.

+Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `vendor/` or `node_modules/` packages never shadow it.
+- `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
+- A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
+- `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
+- Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.
+- A forge repository other than `origin`'s GitHub repository is refused.
+- The written config holds only answers: no `[changesets]`, `[cascade]`, or `[init]` defaults.

+Add discoverable --help surface (8 user commands, plumbing hidden), NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR-driven color and box-drawing tables for status and release --dry-run, and remove schema-version text from default output.
+**`callisto release` replaces the legacy publish commands**

+`callisto release` publishes, tags, and creates GitHub releases for every package whose current version has no tag, from any branch with a clean worktree. `--dry-run` previews the plan anywhere; `--package` restricts it and keeps fixed and linked group members together; an unreleased runtime, optional, or peer dependency must be selected with its dependent; credentials (including alternate cargo registries, credential providers, `.npmrc` and `.pypirc`) are checked before the first effect; the receipt goes to the platform state dir or `--receipt`, never inside the checkout.
+- Removed `callisto publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag` (including `--floating-major`), and `filter-plan`. Use `callisto release` or `callisto release --dry-run`.

+- Removed graph `plan_publish`, `filter_plan_by_report`, `create_tags`, `toposort::publish_order`; moon extension `plan-publish` is now `release`, and removed names error instead of falling back to `status`.

+- `release plan --package` now also keeps config-declared linked-group members, and both routes refuse an unselected unreleased dependency (`ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason::DependencyNotSelected`, was `PlatformDependencyNotSelected`).
+- Release decisions are written as schema 2 (adds `unreleasedVersion`). Schema 1 files still read; an earlier build cannot read a schema-2 decision.

The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`; npm workspaces also set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so publishes carry provenance), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.

-`callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the accepted values. Its environment-setup step no longer references sibling action `setup-callisto` through `uses:` (`$/` and an external `owner/repo/path@ref` both resolve against whichever ref invoked the *top-level* workflow, not necessarily this action's own) -- it now calls `setup-callisto`'s install script directly by `github.action_path`, so it always uses its own checked-out ref, including when invoked from another repository's workflow.

-`init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.

-Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `vendor/` or `node_modules/` packages never shadow it.
-- `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
-- A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
-- `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
-- Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.
-- A forge repository other than `origin`'s GitHub repository is refused.
-- The written config holds only answers: no `[changesets]`, `[cascade]`, or `[init]` defaults.

-Add discoverable --help surface (8 user commands, plumbing hidden), NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR-driven color and box-drawing tables for status and release --dry-run, and remove schema-version text from default output.
-**`callisto release` replaces the legacy publish commands**

-`callisto release` publishes, tags, and creates GitHub releases for every package whose current version has no tag, from any branch with a clean worktree. `--dry-run` previews the plan anywhere; `--package` restricts it and keeps fixed and linked group members together; an unreleased runtime, optional, or peer dependency must be selected with its dependent; credentials (including alternate cargo registries, credential providers, `.npmrc` and `.pypirc`) are checked before the first effect; the receipt goes to the platform state dir or `--receipt`, never inside the checkout.

lines: +**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

+Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.

+`callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (the workflow path release artifact attestations are bound to) for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`/`--no-workflow` (mutually exclusive), refuses to overwrite an existing file (checked before the preview, including under `--dry-run`). After writing the file, init prints that a merge to the default branch publishes, so that branch should require pull requests and reviews. JSON output carries the same text as a `workflow-merge-publishes` diagnostic with the new `info` severity. The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`; npm workspaces also set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so publishes carry provenance), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.

+`callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the accepted values. Its environment-setup step no longer references sibling action `setup-callisto` through `uses:` (`$/` and an external `owner/repo/path@ref` both resolve against whichever ref invoked the *top-level* workflow, not necessarily this action's own) -- it now calls `setup-callisto`'s install script directly by `github.action_path`, so it always uses its own checked-out ref, including when invoked from another repository's workflow.
+**`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**

+`init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.

+Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `vendor/` or `node_modules/` packages never shadow it.
+- `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
+- A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
+- `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
+- Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.
+- A forge repository other than `origin`'s GitHub repository is refused.
+- The written config holds only answers: no `[changesets]`, `[cascade]`, or `[init]` defaults.

+Add discoverable --help surface (8 user commands, plumbing hidden), NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR-driven color and box-drawing tables for status and release --dry-run, and remove schema-version text from default output.
+**`callisto release` replaces the legacy publish commands**

+`callisto release` publishes, tags, and creates GitHub releases for every package whose current version has no tag, from any branch with a clean worktree. `--dry-run` previews the plan anywhere; `--package` restricts it and keeps fixed and linked group members together; an unreleased runtime, optional, or peer dependency must be selected with its dependent; credentials (including alternate cargo registries, credential providers, `.npmrc` and `.pypirc`) are checked before the first effect; the receipt goes to the platform state dir or `--receipt`, never inside the checkout.
+- Removed `callisto publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag` (including `--floating-major`), and `filter-plan`. Use `callisto release` or `callisto release --dry-run`.

+- Removed graph `plan_publish`, `filter_plan_by_report`, `create_tags`, `toposort::publish_order`; moon extension `plan-publish` is now `release`, and removed names error instead of falling back to `status`.

+- `release plan --package` now also keeps config-declared linked-group members, and both routes refuse an unselected unreleased dependency (`ReleaseSelectionInvalidReason::DependencyNotSelected`, was `PlatformDependencyNotSelected`).
+- Release decisions are written as schema 2 (adds `unreleasedVersion`). Schema 1 files still read; an earlier build cannot read a schema-2 decision.

lines: -**PyPI publish stops forcing `--skip-existing` against private indexes**

-Twine 5+ refuses to run at all with that flag against any repository other than the public warehouses (`upload.pypi.org` / `test.pypi.org`), so it's now included only when the target is one of those.

-`callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (the workflow path release artifact attestations are bound to) for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`/`--no-workflow` (mutually exclusive), refuses to overwrite an existing file (checked before the preview, including under `--dry-run`). After writing the file, init prints that a merge to the default branch publishes, so that branch should require pull requests and reviews. JSON output carries the same text as a `workflow-merge-publishes` diagnostic with the new `info` severity. The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`; npm workspaces also set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so publishes carry provenance), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.

-`callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the accepted values. Its environment-setup step no longer references sibling action `setup-callisto` through `uses:` (`$/` and an external `owner/repo/path@ref` both resolve against whichever ref invoked the *top-level* workflow, not necessarily this action's own) -- it now calls `setup-callisto`'s install script directly by `github.action_path`, so it always uses its own checked-out ref, including when invoked from another repository's workflow.
-**`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**

-`init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.

-Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `vendor/` or `node_modules/` packages never shadow it.
-- `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
-- A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
-- `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
-- Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.
-- A forge repository other than `origin`'s GitHub repository is refused.
-- The written config holds only answers: no `[changesets]`, `[cascade]`, or `[init]` defaults.
-Install callisto with proto: `proto/callisto.toml` downloads the release binary for macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 (glibc or musl). moon tasks run the installed CLI.
-- Removed the moon extension (`callisto-moon` crate) and the `callisto-moon.wasm` release asset. Use the proto plugin and run `callisto` from moon tasks.

-- Removed the moon project-graph cross-check: `ProjectLocator::declared_edges`, `DeclaredEdge`, `DeclaredEdgeKind`, `DiagnosticCode::GraphEdgeDisagreement` and `LocateError::{MoonUnavailable, MoonOutputParse, IncompatibleMoonVersion}`.
-- Removed `IdentityResolver` and its errors `GraphError::UnsupportedIdentityEcosystem` (E155) and `GraphError::PackageIdentifierParse` (E156); the `callisto-cli` `wrapper` feature is gone.

-Add discoverable --help surface (8 user commands, plumbing hidden), NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR-driven color and box-drawing tables for status and release --dry-run, and remove schema-version text from default output.
